screen_html.probe: every tick reads the verb off the live adapter, never a version number (_html_verb): the public edit_message when inspect.signature shows a parameter named parse_mode (positional-or-keyword or keyword-only; **kwargs does not count), else the adapter's own coroutine _edit_text, else none. The HTML form goes through that verb (edit_message(chat, message_id, html, parse_mode='HTML') and its SendResult, or _edit_text(chat, message_id, html, 'HTML') which raises on refusal); on any refusal other than 'not modified' the same tick edits plain through the public edit_message. Plain succeeded right after HTML failed = the HTML form was refused: screen_format 'plain', the reason in html_error (the exception class, or 'edit_message: <error>'), HTML tried again after HTML_RETRY_TICKS (12). No verb at all = plain, html_error 'no HTML verb (edit_message without parse_mode, no _edit_text)'. The record names the verb that carries the HTML: html_verb 'edit_message' | '_edit_text' | null
screen_html.contract: TelegramAdapter.edit_message(self, chat_id, message_id, content, *, finalize=False, metadata=None) -> SendResult: no parse_mode on any engine known today; without finalize it calls _edit_text(chat_id, message_id, content), plain text. TelegramAdapter._edit_text(self, chat_id: str, message_id: str, text: str, parse_mode: Any = None) -> None: normalizes the ids, passes parse_mode to Bot.edit_message_text only when given, raises the PTB error on refusal ('Message is not modified' included). A PRIVATE method: the plugin treats it as a capability, never as a promise, asks the public verb's signature first (the catalog review's order) and keeps the plain public edit as the fallback. The parse mode is the string 'HTML' (ParseMode.HTML is that string); the markup is <b> and one <blockquote expandable>, both Bot API 7.4+, not the rich_message parameter

kimi_quota.caveat: the request never goes through the credential pool's rotation, so a failed request cannot mark the pool exhausted; which windows the account has (weekly on legacy plans, monthly on new ones) is the provider's answer, not a setting. The resolver is Hermes' own auth code: without a usable key in .env or the gateway's environment it loads the pool, and loading saves the pool to auth.json once when it changes something (for example a placeholder key in .env seeded into the pool, a row an older Hermes wrote with the secret in it, an emptied auth_type), the save Hermes makes itself the first time it loads that pool; the plugin's own code writes nothing there. The request follows no redirect (quota_cache.http_get, tests/test_quota_cache.py)

hermes_version.probe: the version of the code the gateway imported at start-up, looked up in sys.modules, never imported: hermes_cli.__version__ as a value of the module (0.21.1-0.21.5); else hermes_cli.version_info._cached_version_info.base_version, the identity the gateway resolved at start-up (0.21.6: no I/O, no git, an update on disk does not rename the running code); else the module's __getattr__, which reads the install stamp, any error of it 'version lookup failed'; 0.0.0 or unknown = 'no version stamp on this installation'; absent = no data (not on this installation). Never importlib.metadata (an editable install keeps the dist-info of install time), never hermes_cli.build_info.get_code_identity(refresh=True) (it would restamp the running gateway's code_sha)
hermes_version.contract: GET https://api.github.com/repos/NousResearch/hermes-agent/releases/latest with If-None-Match (the last answer's ETag), no token, at most once per 15 minutes (release_cache in the plugin record), in the plugin's own worker under a 25 s deadline; /releases?per_page=100 only when Latest names another version than the last answer (a new ETag alone is notes edited after publication). A failed check keeps the last answer with its reason and the time it was confirmed; fewer than 10 requests left in GitHub's window, or none, waits for its reset (Retry-After first, an hour at most). Without a token a 304 counts against the 60 an hour (measured 2026-10-08), so the cadence is the budget: 4 an hour plus a list per release. Version from the release name 'Hermes Agent vX.Y.Z', else a tag in the release scheme (v0.21.6), never a date tag (v2026.9.24); releases behind = position on the list (drafts and pre-releases skipped), never arithmetic on version numbers. Not a source: moves neither the status nor the coverage. The engine's banner.check_for_updates (commits behind main) is not used

external_limits.probe: limits_sources in the config, a list of up to 4 entries checked when the settings are read: url http on loopback (127.0.0.1, localhost, [::1]) without credentials; key_env a variable name that is not a bot token variable (TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN, HERMES_DASHBOARD_BOT_TOKEN, any *_BOT_TOKEN in any case); timeout_seconds 1..120, default 20. A refused entry is 'no data' with its reason and is never requested; limits_enabled off = no sources
external_limits.contract: contract 1 (README, External limit sources): GET <url> with Accept application/json and an optional Authorization Bearer from key_env; 200, a JSON object of at most 64 KB with contract, provider, state ok|login_expired|unavailable, reason, plan, login_expires_at, fetched_at, windows[] (up to 6: used_percent, resets_at, scope, severity, label); unknown keys ignored, every string sanitized. No proxy from the environment, no redirect, the body of an error answer unread. The tick waits 25 s; the request runs on in its own worker (one per source) with timeout_seconds; on a miss the last line with its own stamp while younger than two ticks or two limits_refresh_seconds. One attempt per limits_refresh_seconds, cache in the plugin record under external_cache (external.py, collect.py)

gemini_log.probe: HERMES_HOME/logs/ is a directory: no directory = unsupported; the directory without errors.log = fresh with no 429 (the engine on Windows creates the file at the first WARNING); a file that cannot be read or is not UTF-8 = unavailable, the line keeps the last 429 the record remembers; limits_enabled off = not read
reads: the whole of logs/errors.log on the first read, if the file is at most 4 MB and decodes as UTF-8 (every read is a first read until one succeeds and leaves last_429 in the record, null when nothing was seen); otherwise, and after that, its last 256 KB, from the first whole line to the last
the stamp, level and logger of every entry header
for an entry whose first line holds Gemini and HTTP 429: limit: N, model: X and retry in N s of its message, the traceback excluded
entries within 10 s of the newest as one refusal
never_reads: the text of a message beyond those three fields
gemini_log.contract: hermes_logging.py: errors.log holds WARNING and above, rotated at 2 MB with 2 backups (:196), UTF-8, format '%(asctime)s %(levelname)s%(session_tag)s %(name)s: %(message)s' (:47), the stamp naive in the host's local time. The text-to-speech 429: ERROR tools.tts_tool 'TTS generation failed (gemini): Gemini TTS API error (HTTP 429): <error.message>' with its traceback (tools/tts_tool.py:310-314, tools/tts_tool_providers.py:603), repeated within the same second by the executor's WARNING cut at 200 characters (agent/tool_executor.py:994) and the voice reply's WARNING (gateway/run_voice.py:342); the LLM path: WARNING agent.conversation_loop 'API call failed ... summary=Gemini HTTP 429 (RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED): ...' (agent/turn_recovery.py:916-919, agent/gemini_native_adapter.py:628); the streamed call: ERROR agent.chat_completion_helpers 'Streaming failed before delivery: Gemini HTTP 429 (RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED): ...' with its traceback (agent/chat_completion_helpers.py:3150), beside the turn loop's WARNING 'Retrying API call in Ns' (agent/turn_recovery.py:1091-1095), the engine's own backoff and not Google's retry. QuotaFailure and RetryInfo are dropped by the engine: only the message is logged. The last 429 is kept in the plugin record (gemini_log_cache); a retry over 120 s is the daily quota, an event until the reset; any other 429 marks the line for an hour; no network (gemini_log.py)

gemini_log.caveat: only the engine's own calls are in that log: a script that calls Gemini on its own, such as a skill's, is not seen. The stamp is converted with the process's own zone, so the hour repeated when summer time ends adds an hour to the age of a 429 from that hour. The engine on Windows opens the file lazily: until the first WARNING there is no file, which reads as no 429. A daily quota spent just before Google's reset asks for a short retry and marks the line only

reads: jobs[].id, name, enabled, state, paused_at, next_run_at, last_run_at, last_status, failure_streak
the KIND of last_error and last_delivery_error in a word (cron_jobs.error_kind), never the text

cron.contract: cron/jobs.py: jobs.json written atomically (mkstemp + rename) with the outcome of the LAST run per job: last_status in the documented closed set ok | error | delivery_failed | blocked_config plus delivery_queued (cron/scheduler.py), last_error, last_delivery_error, failure_streak (agent failures in a row; delivery failures are not counted), state scheduled | paused | completed | running | error. The ticker writes ticker_heartbeat every loop (60 s), ticker_last_success on a loop without an exception, ticker_last_error with the epoch on its first line and the text after it. The thresholds are the engine's own (hermes cron status): a heartbeat older than three ticks plus slack, 200 s, is a dead ticker; a next_run_at more than 15 min in the past with a live ticker is a job that is not firing. The engine's error texts are reduced to the kind of the error in a word in the order of the engine's own health projection (agent/monitoring/cron_health.py: auth, rate limit, timeout, network), then the Telegram delivery answers and the ticker's own failures; a last_status literal the plugin does not know is named as it is and is never green. A failure a later ok run replaced in jobs.json stays in the details for two ticks (cron_cache.held). The layered order of the checks (ticker alive, record consistent, run recorded, delivery confirmed) follows itpartypattaya/hermes-cron's cron-doctor (MIT); no code is taken from it. A job fires only when enabled and without a pause marker, the paused state or a paused_at stamp (is_job_runnable, _has_pause_marker); an enabled record with the stamp alone is a half-pause the ticker self-disables on its next loop (0.9.1 reads it as paused, never overdue), while hermes cron list and hermes cron status read it by enabled alone; the three fields are read as the ticker reads them (0.9.2): enabled and paused_at by their truth (null is off, a number is a stamp), the state as written (Paused is no pause marker, and a job the ticker may fire is active whatever its state short of completed)

telegram_traffic.contract: One public property (send_path_degraded, declared on BasePlatformAdapter and overridden by the Telegram adapter) and four private attributes of TelegramAdapter, read as attributes of the live object, never called (no method of the adapter is invoked). plugins/platforms/telegram/adapter.py: is_connected is self._running (the adapter was started), which says nothing about updates arriving or replies leaving; the adapter counts for itself: _updates_received_total grows with every update Telegram hands to getUpdates in the current polling generation (kept for hermes-agent#102260), _polling_generation and _polling_generation_started_monotonic reset on every reconnect, _polling_last_progress_monotonic is the last successful getUpdates round-trip, send_path_degraded (the public property over the adapter's private flag) makes send() answer SendResult(success=False, error='send_path_degraded') until the generation proves progress, and _edit_text does not check it, so the dashboard's own edit can move while every reply fails. Verdicts: the send path degraded past a 120 s reconnect grace = no sends (critical); no polling progress for 300 s = stalled (critical); no update seen for longer than twice the longest gap of the last 7 days, at least 6 h and at most 48 h, and only after a first update was seen = quiet (warning); three or more failed sends in the last hour = an event. The counter is read once per tick, so 'last update seen' is the tick that saw it grow. A failed send is the engine's own ERROR line 'Failed to send Telegram message' in logs/errors.log; successes are not logged at that level, so the last successful send the plugin can vouch for is its own confirmed edit (Confirmed in the details). The record (traffic_cache): generation, received_total, last_update_seen_at, gaps per day, degraded_since, last_send_error_at

context_files.contract:
The engine builds a session's system prompt on its first turn and keeps it (agent/conversation_loop.py restore_or_build, hermes_state_sessions.py update_system_prompt): a snapshot, rebuilt in place after a compression or a model switch, a new row after /new. Context files go in as '## <label>

<stripped text>' right after '# Project Context

The following project context files have been loaded and should be followed:

' (build_context_files_prompt), first kind found wins, each capped by context_file_max_chars with a head 70 % / tail 20 % cut and a '[...truncated <name>: kept H+T of N chars' marker, a chain capped again as 'AGENTS.md (directory chain)', the cursor rules as one bundle; the scan replaces a refused file's text with '[BLOCKED: <label> contained potential prompt injection'. sessions.cwd is NULL for gateway sessions (run_agent._launch_cwd_for_session sets it for the CLI only); the directory searched is resolve_agent_cwd(), which the prompt's runtime block names. The verdict renders the files found on disk the engine's way and compares them with the block: the same text loaded, the engine's cut of that text truncated, the notice blocked, anything else outdated; when the prompt holds the current text, the engine's next part right after it (the skills index '## Skills
Before replying, scan the skills below', 'Workspace (snapshot at session start', the memory block's 46 '═', 'Conversation started: ', the runtime heading; the same on 0.21.1, 0.21.3, 0.21.5 and main) proves the block ended there; without that proof a file changed after the session started (the newest of the file's and the link's mtime; a time ahead of the clock is none) is outdated. A context file the engine skips because it is not UTF-8 is not loaded, named so; a prompt with rules and no directory to compare them with is unknown. The prompt and the files never leave the worker (collect._rules_guarded, the tick's deadline)
